problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{4}{{s}^{3}}.$

feedback.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{3!}{{s}^{3+1}}=\frac{6}{{s}^{4}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{6}{{s}^{4}} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{t}^{3}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {t}^{3} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} & ={t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}}={L}^{-1}{-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}}=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
